summary: This is a clean, well-scoped increment adding a Task Execution Trace (TET) core service and a client-facing security shield gate, with no live route wiring yet. The new compliance.task_execution_traces migration (0268) matches the established org-scoped RLS template verbatim (identical to 0197_prompt_cache_metrics.sql: app_runtime_org_scoped + service_role_bypass policies, correct GRANTs), schema.ts's export matches the migration column-for-column, and the migration index/journal entry (idx 265) does not collide with any other migration in the sequence (0265-0268 are all distinct, sequential). task-execution-trace-service.ts correctly reuses withTenantContext (userId is optional there by design, so getTrace/listTraces passing only orgId is valid, not a bug) and the update/insert/query chains match this repo's real Drizzle usage patterns exactly (verified against sibling services). tet-shield-gate.ts reuses the existing prompt-security layer1/layer3 functions with real, verified signatures, fails closed on a Layer 3 network error, and its malicious-only block condition (ignoring the 'suspicious' verdict) is consistent with the existing defense-in-depth.ts's own established behavior, not a new gap. The test file's fake DB double correctly models the real update().set().where().returning() chain shape. Diff touches drizzle/*.sql and schema.ts, correctly placing it at tier2 per the deterministic path-based classifier; no .github/workflows/** files are touched. No route/API surface is wired to this service yet, so the change's live blast radius is effectively zero pending a future increment.
issues: getTrace()/listTraces() only scope reads by orgId, not userId, so once a future route wires this in, any authenticated user in an org could read another org member's trace records (which may contain sensitive action text/PII/blocked-prompt content) unless the eventual API route adds its own userId filter -- worth flagging for whoever wires the first consumer, not a blocking defect in this increment since no route exists yet.

ai-os/boss/ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml still lists this task's claim under `active:` even though PROGRESS.md documents it as fully complete and verified -- should be moved to recently_completed per that file's own protocol, minor process hygiene gap only.
